citation.authors: Dreifus EM, Burke OM, Alexis AF et al
citation.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology

cited_by.title: Laser hair removal on dark skin

record.design: Clinical review of lasers and energy devices
record.finding: Melanin competes for laser energy in skin of colour, raising the risk of dark or pale marks, blisters and scarring; optimal outcomes need careful pre- and post-treatment care, strict photoprotection and sequential, lower-energy treatments; large prospective trials in darker skin are lacking.
record.note: Same review as in the stretch marks entry.

record.design: Clinical review of laser and energy device safety
record.finding: In skin of colour, melanin competes for the laser energy and raises the risk of dark or pale marks, blisters and scarring. Low-fluence Q-switched and picosecond Nd:YAG are favourable; non-ablative fractional lasers can be used conservatively; ablative devices carry more complications. The authors say large prospective trials in darker skin are lacking.
record.note: Published online 27 Aug 2026; covers Fitzpatrick IV-VI, not only Black skin.
